text:
Kira Thompson: Flagging an enterprise Q that came in via AEs (Bank of Northlake security team). They’re asking very specifically:
1) rotation frequency (what we do by default + can customer mandate cadence)
2) evidence requirements (what artifacts/logs we can provide to prove rotation happened)

Kira Thompson: They also asked if we can “attest” that rotation is completed for customer-managed KMS keys in Private, and what our runbook looks like during emergency rotation.

Kira Thompson: Draft Q&A doc we’ve been iterating on (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/security-and-compliance/kms-rotation-customer-qna-draft (internal)

Naomi Feldman: +1 this is coming up in multiple deals. We need a consistent answer that doesn’t over-promise for Private (customer-managed keys).

Elliot Price: For public-facing docs, we’re about to land the rotation + troubleshooting pages via docs PR. (still in review)
https://github.com/redwood-docs/pull/1187
We can link prospects to the cleaned-up version once merged; until then keep it “draft / under review.”

Marcus Lin: On #1: We should separate “scheduled rotation” vs “emergency rotation.”
- Scheduled: recommended cadence (we’ve been using 90 days as the baseline rec), but customer can choose tighter. Hosted/Dedicated we can enforce in control plane; Private is “supported workflow” with shared responsibility.
- Emergency: rotate ASAP, bounded by operational window + validation. For Hosted/Dedicated we can do same-day. For Private, depends on customer change control but we can provide steps + support.

Olga Petrov: For #2 evidence: we should be explicit what is evidence vs what is an “attestation.” We can provide:
- Audit events from our audit pipeline (key lifecycle + decrypt failures etc)
- Change management record (ticket/change request ID) for Hosted/Dedicated rotations
- For Private, we can provide the runbook + what signals to capture, but the customer’s KMS audit logs live in their cloud account.
Also: map to SOC2/ISO control language (e.g., key mgmt, logging/monitoring) and avoid absolute statements.

Daniel Carter: If they’re asking “prove rotation happened,” we can propose a standard evidence bundle:
- Export of KMS-related audit events for the relevant window (tenant-scoped where possible)
- Screenshot/CSV from metrics dashboard showing key-version usage shift (new key use ramping, old key decrypt fallback going to zero)
- If re-encryption job exists for artifact types: job ID + completion timestamp
- Exception log: any decrypt failures during window + resolution

Connor O'Brien: Also important: “rotation complete” definition we’ve been aligning on internally is “new writes use new key immediately; reads allow dual-read for bounded time; completion = no remaining ciphertext requiring old key in active paths OR old-key usage is below threshold and explicitly accepted.” We should keep the wording tight.

Simran Kaur: For Private deployments: we should not claim we can rotate customer-managed KEKs ourselves. We can say:
- Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for KEK
- Customer rotates the KEK per their org policy
- Redwood supports a dual-read window (new key first, fallback old) to reduce downtime, plus guidance on re-encrypting stored artifacts (where applicable)
- Redwood can assist in validation (health endpoint / logs), but customer retains control of KMS + KMS audit logs

Kira Thompson: Do we have a canonical list of audit events we can cite? The prospect asked for “sample event names/fields.”

Marcus Lin: Yep, use the audit logging spec page (internal for now). It enumerates events like key rotation initiated/completed, decrypt failures, AccessDenied, etc.
Confluence: https://redwoodinference.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Security/pages/XXX/kms-key-lifecycle-audit-events
(If sharing externally, we should share a redacted excerpt / table, not the whole internal page.)

Elliot Price: We can add an “Enterprise appendix” section to the docs that lists the event types + example payload fields, and mark it as “available on request.” But we need Security/GRC sign-off on what’s safe to publish.

Olga Petrov: Agreed. Also ensure we’re not leaking internal IDs or anything that could be used for recon. In evidence bundles, we should:
- allow key aliases but not raw key material
- key IDs may be partially redacted (last 6-8 chars) unless the customer requests full and it’s approved
- include tenant ID only if it’s their own tenant

Dr. Aisha Rahman: Please keep the response crisp and consistent with shared responsibility. For Bank of Northlake, they will want “what do you do by default” + “what can we configure” + “what do you hand us during audit.” Don’t bury the lead.

Kira Thompson: Proposed response draft (please poke holes):

“Rotation frequency:
- Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood supports scheduled rotation and can align with customer policy; our recommended cadence is at least every 90 days, with the ability to perform emergency rotation as needed.
- Private (customer-managed KMS): Redwood provides a supported rotation procedure and validation steps. The customer controls the KMS key and can rotate per their internal policy; Redwood’s platform is designed to tolerate rotation with a bounded dual-read period to minimize downtime.

Evidence:
- Redwood can provide audit logs and operational evidence showing key usage and rotation activity in Redwood-managed environments.
- For Private with customer-managed keys, KMS provider audit logs (e.g., CloudTrail) are generated in the customer’s account; Redwood can provide platform-side logs/metrics that indicate successful decrypt/encrypt behavior, plus the operator runbook and validation checklist.”

Kira Thompson: Also planning to attach (or link) the rotation procedure + audit event list excerpt once Elliot confirms what’s publishable.

Marcus Lin: Looks good. Small tweak: don’t say “at least every 90 days” as if it’s a guarantee; say “we recommend 90 days; cadence is configurable by contract/policy.” Also explicitly mention that emergency rotation is supported and tested, and that there may be a short dual-read overlap.

Daniel Carter: +1. For “evidence,” suggest listing concrete artifacts:
- Timestamped audit events for encrypt/decrypt/rotation
- Change record ID (for Redwood-managed)
- For Private: validation output (health endpoint results, decrypt success rates, and confirmation that old-key fallback has ceased within the agreed window)

Connor O'Brien: We should add: “If you require a formal rotation report, we can provide one on request as part of enterprise support.” That’s been asked before.

Olga Petrov: Yes, but phrase as “can provide an evidence package / report upon request” and avoid “formal attestation” language unless Legal approves.

Elliot Price: Re publishable links: For now we can share the draft Drive Q&A + a PDF export of the runbook (restricted). Once docs PR merges, we can share the public docs page and keep the detailed checklist behind our enterprise portal.

Kira Thompson: Action items:
- I’ll update the response with the recommended/contractual wording and include an evidence bundle outline.
- @Olga Petrov / @Daniel Carter can you review the “evidence” section for control-mapping language?
- @Marcus Lin can you sanity-check the rotation frequency wording?

Support Bot: Reminder set by Kira Thompson: “Send vetted response to AE + attach evidence bundle outline” in 1 day.

Olga Petrov: I’ll review today. Please include a single sentence on shared responsibility for Private: “Customer manages KMS key lifecycle; Redwood manages application encryption behavior and provides operational guidance.”

Marcus Lin: Will review. Also: avoid saying “zero downtime” — say “designed to minimize downtime; bounded dual-read window.”

Kira Thompson: Got it. Will send final to AE after edits + approvals.
